provisions.title: Lawful processing: consent or certain legitimate uses
provisions.text: (1) A person may process the personal data of a Data Principal only in accordance with the provisions of this Act and for a lawful purpose,— (a) for which the Data Principal has given her consent; or (b) for certain legitimate uses.

provisions.title: Standard of consent
provisions.text: (1) The consent given by the Data Principal shall be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, and shall signify an agreement to the processing of her personal data for the specified purpose and be limited to such personal data as is necessary for such specified purpose.

provisions.title: Certain legitimate uses
provisions.text: A Data Fiduciary may process personal data of a Data Principal for any of following uses, namely:— (a) for the specified purpose for which the Data Principal has voluntarily provided her personal data to the Data Fiduciary, and in respect of which she has not indicated to the Data Fiduciary that she does not consent to the use of her personal data.

provisions.title: Right to withdraw consent
provisions.text: (4) Where consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing of personal data, such Data Principal shall have the right to withdraw her consent at any time, with the ease of doing so being comparable to the ease with which such consent was given.

provisions.title: Notice given by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal
provisions.text: (i) withdraw her consent, with the ease of doing so being comparable to that with which such consent was given;

provisions.title: Cessation of processing after withdrawal
provisions.text: (6) If a Data Principal withdraws her consent to the processing of personal data under sub-section (5), the Data Fiduciary shall, within a reasonable time, cease and cause its Data Processors to cease processing the personal data of such Data Principal unless such processing without her consent is required or authorised under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder or any other law for the time being in force in India.

provisions.title: Erasure by Data Processor
provisions.text: (b) cause its Data Processor to erase any personal data that was made available by the Data Fiduciary for processing to such Data Processor.

provisions.title: Burden of proof for consent
provisions.text: (10) Where a consent given by the Data Principal is the basis of processing of personal data and a question arises in this regard in a proceeding, the Data Fiduciary shall be obliged to prove that a notice was given by her to the Data Principal and consent was given by such Data Principal to the Data Fiduciary in accordance with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.

provisions.title: Notice to accompany or precede a consent request
provisions.text: (1) Every request made to a Data Principal under section 6 for consent shall be accompanied or preceded by a notice given by the Data Fiduciary to the Data Principal, informing her,— (i) the personal data and the purpose for which the same is proposed to be processed; (ii) the manner in which she may exercise her rights under sub-section (4) of section 6 and section 13; and (iii) the manner in which the Data Principal may make a complaint to the Board, in such manner and as may be prescribed.

provisions.title: Language of notice
provisions.text: (3) The Data Fiduciary shall give the Data Principal the option to access the contents of the notice referred to in sub-sections (1) and (2) in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.

provisions.title: Clear and plain request for consent
provisions.text: (3) Every request for consent under the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall be presented to the Data Principal in a clear and plain language, giving her the option to access such request in English or any language specified in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution … authorised by the Data Fiduciary to respond to any communication from the Data Principal for the purpose of exercise of her rights under the provisions of this Act.

provisions.title: Notice given by Data Fiduciary to Data Principal

provisions.title: Erasure of personal data
provisions.text: (7) A Data Fiduciary shall, unless retention is necessary for compliance with any law for the time being in force,— (a) erase personal data, upon the Data Principal withdrawing her consent or as soon as it is reasonable to assume that the specified purpose is no longer being served, whichever is earlier; and … (b) cause its Data Processor to erase any personal data that was made available by the Data Fiduciary for processing to such Data Processor.

provisions.title: General obligations of Data Fiduciary
provisions.text: (1) A Data Fiduciary shall, irrespective of any agreement to the contrary or failure of a Data Principal to carry out the duties provided under this Act, be responsible for complying with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder in respect of any processing undertaken by it or on its behalf by a Data Processor.

provisions.text: 29. (1) No core biometric information, collected or created under this Act, shall be— (a) shared with anyone for any reason whatsoever; or (b) used for any purpose other than generation of Aadhaar numbers and authentication under this Act. … (4) No Aadhaar number or core biometric information collected or created under this Act in respect of an Aadhaar number holder shall be published, displayed or posted publicly, except for the purposes as may be specified by regulations.

provisions.title: Verifiable consent for processing of personal data of child
provisions.text: (1) A Data Fiduciary shall adopt appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure that verifiable consent of the parent is obtained before the processing of any personal data of a child and shall observe due diligence, for checking that the individual identifying herself as the parent is an adult who is identifiable if required in connection with compliance with any law for the time being in force in India, by reference to—

provisions.title: Verifiable parental consent
provisions.text: (1) The Data Fiduciary shall, before processing any personal data of a child or a person with disability who has a lawful guardian obtain verifiable consent of the parent of such child or the lawful guardian, as the case may be, in such manner as may be prescribed. Explanation.—For the purpose of this sub-section, the expression “consent of the parent” includes the consent of lawful guardian, wherever applicable.

provisions.title: Processing of personal data of children
provisions.text: (1) The Data Fiduciary shall, before processing any personal data of a child or a person with disability who has a lawful guardian obtain verifiable consent of the parent of such child or the lawful guardian, as the case may be, in such manner as may be prescribed. Explanation.—For the purpose of this sub-section, the expression “consent of the parent” includes the consent of lawful guardian, wherever applicable.

value.assessment: None of the seven consent criteria can be determined from the supplied Evidence. The graph has one cookie consent banner (banner:frontend/src/index.html:19), which only shows window.cookieconsent.initialise. It also has several Privacy Policy notice paragraphs and a GDPR erasure notice. Every other part is empty: no purposes, grant paths, controls, enforcement points, records, withdrawal paths, processors, processor propagation or operations. Each notice has before_grant null, purpose_ids empty, and itemised and language null, so no notice is linked to any consent request or purpose. One notice treats 'By using the Service, you agree to the collection and use of information', and a later 'consent to this Privacy Policy', as agreement. That reads as implied, bundled consent, which raises a concern under Section 6(1), but there is no link to a purpose or grant path that would support a finding. The Evidence says missing links are not proof of absence, and the instruction is not to infer missing links, so each criterion is marked not determinable rather than not met.

criteria.reason: The records array is empty and no grant path is linked to any storage of consent. Missing links are not proof of absence, so the Evidence cannot show whether consent and the notice behind it are recorded in a way that could prove them.

No purposes are resolved, and every notice has empty purpose_ids and itemised null. The notice at privacy-policy line 24 uses general wording ('provide and improve the Service'; 'By using the Service, you agree'), which suggests bundled consent. Still, no grant path or purpose is linked, so whether consent is specific to a stated purpose cannot be established.
The enforcement_points and controls arrays are empty. The banner initialisation is client-side only, and nothing shows the server checking consent before processing.

The withdrawal_paths and grant_paths arrays are empty, so step counts for giving and withdrawing consent cannot be compared. The data erasure form notice is about account erasure, not about withdrawing consent, and it is not linked to any purpose.
The processors and processor_propagation arrays are empty. Nothing shows a withdrawal or erasure being passed on to any Data Processor, and a dispatched call would not prove deletion anyway.

Every notice has before_grant null and is not linked to the banner or to any grant path. The notices also lack itemised data, purpose links and a language option. Whether a notice accompanies or comes before a consent request cannot be established.

The child_gate and parental_verification states are both not determinable. Age or date-of-birth collection and a child audience were not resolved, and no mechanism for verifiable parental consent was found. The policy says it does not knowingly collect data from anyone under 18, but that statement alone does not settle the question.
